title: stall-hunting-vector-tiling-exploratory-may2025
content:
Summary:

This doc captures an exploratory run of microbenchmarks and field traces focused on a particular class of latency anomalies we've been seeing for INT8 and AWQ kernels under multiplexed workloads: short, bursty stalls that disproportionately affect p95/p99 latency even when mean throughput looks fine. I call the investigation "stall hunting" because root behavior looks like transient vector-lane underutilization caused by tiling + scheduling interactions on recent kernels.

Why this matters:
- Customers see sporadic high tail latency on Dedicated pools for mid-sized models (6B-20B) at realistic multi-user mixes.
- Tail spikes lead to retries and cost overruns due to request amplification.
- Existing quantized kernels deliver great average throughput; we need to reduce the tail without blowing up cost.

Hypothesis (short):
- Kernel vector-tiling choices (tile width / lane packing) interact with multi-request interleaving and the GPU kernel scheduler so that some warps become partially idle.
- When a partially-utilized warp waits on memory or barrier, a short stall cascades to other warps via SM-level resource contention and preemption, producing p95/p99 spikes.
- Effect is stronger for AWQ/GPTQ-style kernels that densify memory access and for FP8 variants that insert conversion overheads.

What we ran (method):
- Hardware: A100 40GB (dgx-a), H100 80GB (dev cluster). Note: H100 showed similar but muted behavior.
- Models: 7B OPT-like, 13B LLaMA-style dense transformer.
- Kernels: baseline FP16 cuBLAS paths, custom INT8 (packed lanes), AWQ reference, GPTQ reference, FP8 reference.
- Workloads: multiplexed clients with Poisson arrival (lambda tuned to mean QPS 40, 80) and short prompts (average 60 tokens).
- Concurrency shapes: single long request mix; many short requests mix (tail-heavy).
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/s, SM occupancy (nvprof/nvtx traces), L2 throughput, instruction mix, warp stall reasons when available (stall_mem, stall_exec).
- Microbench harness: bench-stallhunt-v3 (linked in GH PR).

Key observations (numbers are medians across 10 runs, warm start):

- Baseline FP16:
  - p50=42ms, p95=68ms, p99=120ms, tokens/s=1150
  - SM occupancy steady ~78%, warp-stall dominated by memory in expected proportion.

- INT8 (packed-4 lanes typical):
  - p50=28ms, p95=95ms, p99=240ms, tokens/s=1860
  - Notable: large p99 increase relative to p50 (8.5x slower than p50 at p99).
  - NVPROF: bursts where warp occupancy dips to ~32% for 100-400us windows; stall_exec fraction climbs during those windows.

- AWQ-kernel (dense memory pattern):
  - p50=30ms, p95=110ms, p99=270ms, tokens/s=1720
  - L2 throughput variance higher (coefficient of variation ~0.42 vs 0.18 for FP16).

- GPTQ-kernel (tile-friendly but higher convert ops):
  - p50=33ms, p95=88ms, p99=210ms, tokens/s=1620

- FP8 (narrow accumulator conversion loops):
  - p50=31ms, p95=78ms, p99=190ms, tokens/s=1700
  - FP8 had lower p99 than INT8/AWQ but still higher than FP16.

Interpretation:
- INT8 gives best median throughput but worst tail behavior under multiplexing.
- The p99 spikes align with short windows of reduced warp utilization and increased stall_exec, indicating serialization/SM scheduling behavior, not just memory bandwidth exhaustion.
- AWQ's dense gather patterns exacerbate L2 contention variance, which maps to more frequent stall windows.
- FP8 reduces p99 relative to INT8 in our runs, suggesting the conversion overhead helps by rebalancing instruction/memory phases (oddly creating smoother cadence).

Repro steps for a single assertive run:
- checkout bench harness: git checkout bench/stallhunt-v3
- docker run --gpus all -v $PWD:/work bench-image:2025-05 
- ./bench-run --model 13B --kernel int8-packed4 --arrival poisson --qps 80 --seq 60 --runs 10 --nvtx
- collect nvprof logs under /work/out and run python analyze_stalls.py out/*

Trace excerpts (translated to readable form):
- Typical stall window: 120-350us where warp_active drops from 0.78->0.33 and stall_exec increases from 0.12->0.41; L2 read bandwidth fluctuates +/-40% from mean.

Quick root-cause candidate list (ranked):
1) Tile packing creates micro-imbalances in per-lane instruction timing; some lanes finish early and wait at barrier.
2) Branch divergence from fused-ops path variations (AWQ probe) causing warp serialization.
3) Kernel launch coalescing + SM preemption/policy interacting badly with short per-request kernels.
4) Memory microbursts hitting L2 that lead to short stalls and higher variance.

Actions tried (small patches we already prototyped):
- Reduced tile packing (packed-2 instead of packed-4): significant p99 improvement for INT8 at ~6% throughput loss.
- Lightweight kernel fencing to avoid small interleaved launches; reduced p95 by ~18% but added ~3% CPU overhead on host.
- Inserting an extra interleaved noop instruction to spread convert work (for FP8) smoothed variance slightly.

Tradeoffs summary:
- Packed-4 INT8 best median tokens/s but worst tail. Packed-2 reduces tail but costs throughput (approx 5-8%).
- Kernel fencing helps p95/p99 but could increase host-side queue latency under very high QPS.
- AWQ needs a targeted L2 prefetching or stride-aware load to reduce L2 variance; that requires kernel-level changes.

Immediate recommendations:
1) For Dedicated pools supporting strict latency SLOs, introduce a new "tail-safe" INT8 profile (packed-2, conservative launch coalescing) as an optional quant profile customers can pin.
2) Add kernel-level telemetry: emit short NVTX spans for tile entry/exit + per-kernel lane finish times to help correlate warp-level idles to request timings.
3) Run larger A/B field test across a mix of real traffic with the "tail-safe" profile on 2 Dedicated hosts for two weeks; measure p50/p95/p99 and cost delta.
4) Open a follow-up engineering spike to evaluate an SM-aware scheduler change that avoids preemption of short kernels (INF-2208).

Longer-term ideas:
- Investigate micro-scheduling in the runtime to coalesce requests into tile-aligned batches where lanes stay busy across requests (needs careful tail-safety reasoning).
- Explore a hybrid quant profile that uses FP8 for early layers and INT8 for later layers to exploit FP8's smoothing property and keep median speed.
- Model-aware tiling heuristics: choose packing per-layer based on empirical per-layer finish-distributions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does H100's different SM scheduling reduce real production p99? Initial dev runs show reduced amplitude but still present. Need larger sample.
- Is there an opportunity to fix this entirely from the runtime (scheduling/coalescing) vs kernel-level (tile reshape) tradeoffs?

Next steps (owners):
- Priya: land microprobe NVTX instrumentation (PR linked) and schedule A/B field test (by 2025-06-05).
- Evan: prototype packed-2 build and run expanded bench matrix on H100 (by 2025-05-30).
- Jordan: open INF backlog item for SM-aware scheduler exploration (INF-2208) and write the spec stub.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Watch for correlation with small-memory-footprint prompts that keep KV cache cold — could amplify lane imbalances.
- Patch to runtime queuer to avoid interleaving different quant-kernel types on same SM in tight windows (maybe use placement hints).

Appendix (partial raw outputs):
- Example p99 windows aligned to request ids: [req-4132@15:12:04.223, req-4140@15:12:04.246, req-4151@15:12:04.275] all map to same SM-3 windows in nvprof.
- Small sample perf counters during stall window: warp_cycles_active 320k -> 118k, inst_issued 540k -> 380k, l2_read_bytes ± 40%

If anyone wants to pair on reproducing an especially noisy trace I captured yesterday (trace id stall-20250521-0912) ping me and I'll share the nvprof tarball.

-- Priya
